text: Kondhwa residents, particularly those living near NIBM Road, Parge Nagar, and Kausarbaugh, have long been struggling with severe traffic congestion. With the holy month of Ramzan approaching, locals fear that the situation will worsen significantly, as numerous temporary stalls selling food, clothes, and other items are expected to mushroom across the area. Residents have expressed concerns that already heavy congestion, combined with increased noise and air pollution, will make daily life extremely challenging. For months, citizens have repeatedly appealed to PMC to take action against illegal encroachments including roadside food carts using wooden tandoors, gas cylinders placed on roads, and stalls blocking pedestrian pathways. Senior Police Inspector Maya Devre, Kondhwa Traffic Division said the survey was done to appeal to people to follow rules. Corporator Kashif Sayyed committed to deploying 20 volunteers throughout the month controlling traffic across Ward 19. Officials including DCP Traffic Himmat Jadhav, DCP Zone 5 Rajlakshmi Shivankar, ACP Namrata Desai, SPI Kumar Ghadge visited on-site.

text: Residents from NIBM, Undri, and surrounding areas staged a protest near Bizzbay Mall on Saturday evening, opposing the proposed Development Plan (DP) road connecting NIBM Road to Kondhwa Road, citing major safety concerns. The demonstration, held at around 5:30 PM, saw participation from several housing societies and local citizens who raised objections to the road's design and alignment. Protesters warned that the planned merging point near Bizzbay Mall could become a traffic bottleneck, increasing congestion and raising the likelihood of accidents. Residents expressed particular concern over the steep gradient of the proposed stretch. According to a road safety assessment conducted by Global Traffic Solutions, the 375-metre section has gradients ranging between 10.6% and 13.7%, significantly higher than the 4% limit recommended by the Indian Roads Congress. The area already witnesses heavy traffic, with over 63,000 vehicles passing through the nearby intersection daily. Between 2022 and 2024, at least 13 accidents, including four fatalities, have been reported in the vicinity. Residents also highlighted the poor condition of existing roads in the area, including potholes and debris.

text: Residents living near Anandpur Charitable Trust Road, particularly from Ashwini Classic and Nivedita Garden Condominium, are expressing frustration over drainage pipes left unattended on the roadside for weeks. They are scratching and damaging our vehicles, especially two-wheelers, as there is little space left to maneuver. The narrowed road is forcing us to drive dangerously close to parked vehicles and walls. Another commuter added: During peak hours, the congestion becomes unbearable. The road is already narrow, and these pipes have made it worse. PMC drainage department confirmed there is currently no planned drainage work in the vicinity — meaning the pipes have no official project behind them.
